Use case: stylized-concept / identity-preserve. Create ONE production transparent game asset of a distant light amphibious advertising airplane, ONLY the airplane, no banner or rope. The provided image is a style/color reference for the existing yellow and muted turquoise aircraft in our vintage paper collage surfing game. Redesign it as a believable real small high-wing amphibious floatplane seen almost SIDE-ON in level flight, NOSE POINTING LEFT with a very subtle view of its underside because the viewer is on the water below. Slim fuselage, one straight high wing in perspective, recognizable tail fin and horizontal tail, single nose propeller with a restrained translucent motion blur, two slender realistic parallel floats under the fuselage connected by thin struts. The floats may have small retracted amphibious wheel housings, but do not show extended wheels. Correct coherent aircraft anatomy and flight geometry. This is a lightweight tourist aircraft at a distance, not a large airliner.
STYLE: restrained vintage photographic cut-paper illustration, natural soft painted shading, aged yellow fuselage with one muted teal stripe, small dark cockpit windows, fine paper grain, a VERY THIN warm ivory cut edge (1-2 pixel appearance at final scale), clean isolated alpha. More realistic side silhouette than the reference's chunky front-facing sticker. Compact body, wings and floats aligned with flight; no oversized foreground propeller, no cartoon speed marks, no thick white outline, no drop shadow, no neon, no 3D plastic.
COMPOSITION: one horizontal airplane, fully visible, nose at left and tail at right, nearly level with a gentle nose-up angle of about 2 degrees. Fit the airplane tightly into a horizontal 3:1 composition with transparent margins. The game will render a tow cable and a separate fluttering advertising banner attached to the tail, so leave the tail tow point identifiable but do NOT draw any rope, banner, flag, lettering or advertisement. Genuine transparent background, no sea, no sky, no sun, no other objects, no text, no second aircraft.
